gloss: bird of deserted places, traditionally pelican
summary: Israel’s food laws place this bird among those excluded from the table. In the psalm it stands for the singer’s isolation, and in the prophets it settles in landscapes emptied of people.

senses.definition: A bird forbidden as food, associated in poetry with wilderness and abandoned buildings. Its species is uncertain.

evidence.note: The bird appears in the list of flying creatures Israel must avoid eating.
The parallel dietary list places it beside the raḥāmāh and the šālāk.
The speaker compares himself to this bird in the wilderness and to another bird in ruins.
The qāʾat and the qippod take possession of devastated Edom.
Both creatures lodge on the capitals of abandoned Nineveh.

evidence.locator: qt, qtˀ noun no. 2, Targum Onkelos Deuteronomy 14:17 and Targum Jonathan Isaiah 34:11

note: The Aramaic form occurs in translations of these same passages and gives no independent description of the bird. The Greek rendering behind ‘pelican’ and the setting behind ‘owl’ help explain the English alternatives. The parallel lines of the psalm describe solitude without specifying the bird’s appearance.
